The Dendra

The Dendra are intelligent, clever, and problem solvers. They will always investigate natural phenomena and wish to explain it. They want to understand the world around them as best they can. Lovers of nature, theyâ€™ll walk the forests for hours observing the way it works from the largest trees and beasts to the smallest fungus and bug, or fly through the skies observing the sky whales and their prey. As technology advances, the Dendra will be able to use it to further explain the natural wonders of Ebos.

As a passive race, theyâ€™ll only engage in violence to protect the forests and knowledge they steward and accumulate. They are lawful-neutral; the squabbles of other races are of no matter to them, as they observe and tend to the forests, innovate in their labs, dissect in their greenhouses, and study; always seeking knowledge and inventions. They excel in the ecological sciences (discoveries, technology, innovation, etc.)

I donâ€™t know what it is about fantasy artwork and hyper-sexualization of humanoids, but it sure is hard finding artwork that isnâ€™t just T&A.

Dendra are extremely long-lived, often living to 1000/1100 years old. Some assume itâ€™s their knowledge of biology and medicines which allow their extremely long life, but it is in fact a gift from Pomme. There was too much knowledge to Master for them to live shorter life spans.

Their cities and villages, although organized, could sometimes seem chaotic to the untrained eye. Plants, vines, flowers and herbs grow from every nook and cranny. There is always some new experiment in breeding or botany. Experiements with new plants for food and medicine are common, as are breeding trials for the domestication of animals for food and other commodities. Hunting takes too much time away from their studies, so although they have the knowledge, few excel in that area. They prefer the understanding of and breeding animals for meat.

They can always find fresh, drinkable water in the forest. They will be the first race to inhabit the city of Gold Leaf in the Golden Forest, and there will be smaller faction in the Rose Colored Forest. As the Ages pass, the Dendra will spread and take on the characteristics of the forests where they live. Those in the Golden Forest will have the characteristic golden hue about them. Golden hair, golden leaves for wings, and a green and yellow body with random viney tendrils.

Dendra strive to live as efficiently and in tune with their surroundings as possible, while still advancing in the sciences of nature. They are masters of camouflage in their own forests and do not engage predators while observing them. Rather than fight, they evade dangers as to not interrupt the lives of the beasts they are observing. As part plant and part beast, and Masters of cultivation of food, they are able to photosynthesize if nothing is available besides fresh water and sunlight. However, they love food; the cultivation of plants and animals for food and the various combinations are considered high science and nearly an art form.

Average height of about 5' 5" (65 inches or 165cm), with wiry frames, and a wingspan of about double their height when fully stretched out. They must stay light to enjoy flying, which is their favorite leisure activity. Because of their extremely long life, breeding is discouraged until one has Mastered at least one science (at about 250 years of age), but, if the species is under duress, breeding is encouraged to continues the family lines. Pregnancy takes only half an Ebos year, but maturation is slow. Families try to encourage certain couplings based on sciences surrounding personalities and genetics, in hope that a successful millennium-long coupling can be arranged, but many among the Dendra love who they will, for they have wild hearts like the beasts of the forest. Dendra mate for life, which is why coupling is frowned upon at a young age before individuals know in which direction their lives will take them, this doesn't account for deaths, and it's not unheard of for widows and widowers to re-mate.

Their honest and inquisitive nature allows them to identify a Forest Keeper among the other trees, although this grants them no additional favor with the Keepers, aside from friendly conversation.
